conclusions.question: Which writeConcern w values does the managed service accept on insert and update, and is a rejected write applied?
conclusions.answer: w:0, w:1 and w:'majority' are accepted on raw insert and update commands, on collection-level WriteConcern objects and through MongoClient(w='majority'), each returning ok:1 with no writeConcernError. w:2 and w:3 (raw, driver and MongoClient(w=2)) are rejected before execution with code 2 BadValue "w value N exceeds the number of data-bearing voting members", with no errorLabels, and the document or update is not applied. The tag w:'myTag' is rejected with code 2 BadValue "Unknown writeConcern w tag: 'myTag'". This matches the DECISIONS reading of the open-source gateway (validated, then ignored; numeric w of 2 or more refused on this HA-disabled cluster).

conclusions.question: Are j:true and j:false accepted, and do they change anything?
conclusions.answer: Accepted silently. {w:1, j:true} and {w:1, j:false} as raw commands, WriteConcern(j=True) and WriteConcern(j=False) (sent as {j:true} and {j:false}) and MongoClient(journal=True) all return ok:1 with no error on insert and update. Nothing observable changes; any difference in journaling cannot be seen from the data plane.

conclusions.question: Is wtimeout / wTimeoutMS 1 honoured?
conclusions.answer: Accepted silently. Raw {w:'majority', wtimeout:1}, WriteConcern(w='majority', wtimeout=1) and MongoClient(w='majority', wTimeoutMS=1, journal=True) succeed on insert and update with no writeConcernError and no WTimeoutError. On a single-node cluster there is no replication wait for the timeout to cut short, so it has no observable effect.

conclusions.question: Is w:0 honoured?
conclusions.answer: Yes, at the protocol level. PyMongo sends w:0 writes as unacknowledged OP_MSG messages (moreToCome, no lsid). Two such inserts followed by an acknowledged find and count on the same server connection succeeded, so the gateway sends no reply to moreToCome messages. The writes were readable within 1 s, and a duplicate _id under w:0 raised nothing, whereas the default write concern raised DuplicateKeyError 11000 (no codeName) "Duplicate key violation on the requested collection: Index '_id_'". A raw db.command insert with writeConcern {w:0} is not sent with moreToCome, so the gateway replies in full ({n:1, ok:1}) and still reports writeErrors code 11000 for a duplicate.

conclusions.question: Which readConcern levels are accepted outside a transaction, and with what effect?
conclusions.answer: local, majority, available, linearizable and snapshot are all accepted on raw find, on driver find_one with ReadConcern objects and on raw aggregate (majority and snapshot), returning the document with ok:1. On this single-node cluster local, majority, available and linearizable have no observable effect. Level parsing is case-sensitive: 'Majority' fails with code 2 BadValue "Invalid readConcern level: 'Majority'". This differs from the DECISIONS settled item, which says (from the open-source gateway source) that available and linearizable are rejected with CommandNotSupported and that snapshot is rejected unless configured. On the managed service those rejections apply only inside transactions.

conclusions.question: Is readConcern snapshot honoured outside a transaction?
conclusions.answer: No. It is accepted, but replies carry no atClusterTime, so a PyMongo snapshot session (start_session(snapshot=True)) cannot pin a point in time: its second read returned a document inserted after the first read. A snapshot cursor with batchSize 2 returned, in a later getMore, a document inserted between batches, exactly as the local control did. An explicit readConcern {level:'snapshot', atClusterTime: ts} fails with code 72 InvalidOptions "readConcern.atClusterTime is not supported". Outside a transaction, snapshot gives at most a per-batch view.

conclusions.question: Which readConcern levels are accepted inside a transaction, compared with documentdb-local?
conclusions.answer: snapshot, majority and local are accepted (find, then commitTransaction ok:1), and the canonical startTransaction(readConcern snapshot, writeConcern w:'majority') with an update commits. available and linearizable fail on the first statement with code 115 CommandNotSupported "'Available' read concern is not supported" and "'Linearizable' read concern is not supported", with no errorLabels. Compared with the open-source transactions-labels test (documentdb-local 0.117), majority and local behave the same, while snapshot is different: the local engine rejected it with code 115 "'Snapshot' read concern is not supported". This settles DECISIONS open item 3 for this cluster: the managed service accepts snapshot in transactions.

conclusions.question: Does readConcern snapshot give a stable snapshot inside a transaction, and what do local and majority give?
conclusions.answer: Snapshot is honoured: in a snapshot transaction, a second read did not see a document inserted or an update committed by another client after the first read. In local and majority transactions, the second read saw both. That is read-committed behaviour: each statement sees data committed before it started. An application that needs repeatable reads inside a transaction must request readConcern snapshot explicitly. (One trial per level.)

conclusions.question: Do causally consistent sessions work?
conclusions.answer: Only because the session never learns an operation time. Data-command replies (insert, update, find, getMore, aggregate, commitTransaction, getDefaultRWConcern and others) carry no operationTime and no $clusterTime; only hello carries operationTime. A PyMongo causal session therefore normally sends no afterClusterTime, and its operations succeed. Once the session has an operation time (hello run with session=s, or s.advance_operation_time(ts), which is MongoDB's way to chain causality across sessions), PyMongo 4.20 adds readConcern {afterClusterTime} to the next reads and writes. Each of them fails with code 20 IllegalOperation "readConcern.afterClusterTime is not supported on this deployment", and the insert is not applied. A raw readConcern {level:'majority', afterClusterTime} fails the same way. This matches the main-branch read_concern.rs reported in DECISIONS, not the release/1.0-RC2 behaviour (silently accepted) described in issue #770.

conclusions.question: Which readPreference modes are accepted on a find, and are they honoured?
conclusions.answer: PyMongo sees one Mongos (hello msg 'isdbgrid', no setName or hosts) and sends $readPreference for every non-primary mode. primary (omitted by the driver, explicit in the raw command), primaryPreferred, secondaryPreferred and nearest are accepted and served by the single endpoint. secondary is rejected, whether set as a collection option, a client option or in a raw command, with code 133 FailedToSatisfyReadPreference "no server available for query with ReadPreference secondary" and no errorLabels. Extras: any tags fail with 133 "no server available for query with specified tag set list"; hedge {enabled:true} fails with 2 BadValue "hedged reads are not supported"; secondaryPreferred with maxStalenessSeconds 90 is accepted; primary with maxStalenessSeconds fails with 9 FailedToParse "mode 'primary' does not allow for 'maxStalenessSeconds'". With HA disabled there is one endpoint, so no routing can be observed. All of this matches DECISIONS.

conclusions.question: What do getDefaultRWConcern and setDefaultRWConcern do?
conclusions.answer: getDefaultRWConcern on admin returns {defaultReadConcern:{level:'majority'}, defaultWriteConcern:{w:'majority', wtimeout:0}, defaultReadConcernSource:'implicit', defaultWriteConcernSource:'implicit', ok:1}, the constant DECISIONS predicted. It is the same with inMemory:true and unchanged after the set attempts. conclusions.question: Does the managed gateway validate these options as the open-source gateway does (DECISIONS open item 8)?
conclusions.answer: Mostly, with one material exception. Every writeConcern, readPreference, getDefaultRWConcern, afterClusterTime and atClusterTime reply matched the codes and messages DECISIONS derived from the main-branch gateway source. The exception is readConcern level validation. DECISIONS says available, linearizable and (unless configured) snapshot are rejected for every command. On the managed service all five levels are accepted outside transactions; available and linearizable are rejected only inside transactions, with exactly the predicted messages; and snapshot is accepted inside transactions. None of the rejections in this test carried errorLabels.

decisions_corrections: DECISIONS topic 9, settled item 'Which readConcern levels are honored?': on the managed service, available, linearizable and snapshot are accepted outside transactions (find, aggregate, driver ReadConcern). The CommandNotSupported rejections apply only inside transactions, and only to available and linearizable; snapshot is accepted in transactions.

DECISIONS topic 9, open item 3: answered for this cluster. readConcern snapshot is accepted in transactions and gives a stable snapshot there. Outside a transaction it is accepted but not point-in-time (no atClusterTime, getMore sees later inserts), and atClusterTime is rejected (72 InvalidOptions).
New fact for the kit: transactions with readConcern local or majority behave read-committed (a later statement sees rows that other clients committed after the transaction's first read).

New fact for the kit: data-command replies carry no operationTime/$clusterTime, and afterClusterTime is rejected (20 IllegalOperation). Causal sessions work only while the session has no operation time; advance_operation_time, or a hello inside the session, breaks every later read and write in that session.
DECISIONS topic 9, open item 4: hello.maxWriteBatchSize is 25000 on this cluster.

Confirmed on the managed service as DECISIONS predicted: the w validation codes and messages, the readPreference rejections (secondary, tags, hedge, primary+maxStalenessSeconds), the getDefaultRWConcern constant and its errors, and setDefaultRWConcern absent (59 CommandNotFound). The afterClusterTime/atClusterTime handling matches main, not RC2.
